While the guy does make some excellent arguments about paid DLC for shooters, it has nothing to do with Battlefield. This problem effects all types of games where expanded content is paid. Just a few weeks ago I played Saints Row 4 with a friend and I had all the DLC while he just had the base game. This issue is solely a problem with publishers like EA who just want to push a fraction of a cent more out of each game regardless of the impact on the community.

I'd like to see more companies take on the model that Rocket League has moved for. While the scale of maps is different, they can still be free while pointless cosmetic options are paid. Or even a minimal cost for maps that can be offset by charging for cosmetic items. It's exactly as he mentioned in the video that there are a ton of things the actual soldiers did for customization. Why not just charge $1 for each thing?

EA? Fuck, son, check out Paradox - they're the worst offender when it comes to DLC. They usually have enough DLC to cost 3-4 times that of the base game, yet for some weird reason they get a free pass. People masturbate to the DLC for Cities: Skylines, yet it adds virtually no content and both DLC packs combined cost more than the base game with more DLC to come. I honestly don't understand why gamers praise them so much when they're the absolute worst offender by far when it comes to DLC galore.

I bought Cities: Skylines and the first DLC on a humble bundle sale right before the second DLC came out. After I read up on Paradox, I realized that I don't want to support that type of company, so I immediately sent in a refund request.

I actually quite like premium, I hope it remains $100 for everything like Battlefield 4. The content was worth it to me as I have dumped 100's of hours in to the game. If it wasn't I wouldn't get premium.
